subject: Post-call: OptiStore deployment & migration kickstart
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@optistore.ai>, Procurement <procurement@optistore.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: OptiStore deployment & migration kickstart

Hi Olivia / team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment. Highlights from our discussion:

- Key priorities you mentioned: predictable latency for customer-facing search, predictable cost per 1k tokens, and an eventual architecture that isolates PHI/PII workflows.
- Current landscape: production traffic today goes to another LLM API (3rd-party provider), plus a small internal k8s/Triton GPU cluster used for heavy experimentation.
- Initial production target: ~120-150 qps peak (bursty), ~2.5–3M tokens/day, p95 latency budget around 250–300ms for short-query flows.

Where Redwood fits (quick): Hosted API (fastest to launch), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool for stable throughput), Private VPC/on‑prem (for data residency and locked-down networks). We discussed tradeoffs; see attached comparison and the migration MAP spreadsheet I’ll upload.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I’ll share: (a) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private one-pager, (b) security summary, (c) migration MAP (attached).
2) Please confirm: steady-state qps, tokens/day, and any compliance/regulatory constraints we should account for (HIPAA/PCI/SOC2).
3) Schedule: technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineering team (60–90m) — propose Tue 23 Jun or Wed 24 Jun.
4) Procurement note: if you need a pricing ballpark for an 8-GPU Dedicated pool vs Hosted with committed discounts, confirm the procurement timeline (you mentioned EoQ).

Attachments: Redwood-Hosted-Dedicated-Comparison.pdf (summary), OptiStore-migration-MAP.xlsx (milestones).

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Vivek for technical follow-ups.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: OptiStore deployment & migration kickstart

On Tue, Jun 15, 2026 at 10:05 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment.

Thanks — adding a technical lens and a practical migration path proposal. High-level recommendation (based on what we heard):

- Phase 0 (Discovery & sizing): collect real traffic traces (token distribution, seq lengths), sample prompts, current latency percentiles, and recent error patterns. This informs kernel selection and batching strategy.

- Phase 1 (PoC — Dedicated): spin up an 8-GPU Dedicated pool and run a 2-week bench + shadow test against current API. Dedicated gives: predictable latency, isolation from noisy neighbors, and a clearer cost model for sustained workloads. Start with a quantization-friendly variant if model size is large.

- Phase 2 (Gradual migration + Private option): for regulated or high-PII flows, we can run Private VPC alongside Dedicated and route sensitive requests there. Private is heavier ops but required if you must manage keys/data residency.

Migration considerations / blockers to confirm:
- Tokenization parity and prompt/response deltas (we should compare a 1000-sample prompt set).
- KV-cache warming / prefix caching — cold-start cost if requests are highly unique.
- Model fallback policy during rollouts (Hosted fallback vs retry to old provider).
- Ingress bandwidth and egress cost for your region.

Actionable asks for OptiStore before PoC:
- A 48–72h sample of request traces (anonymized) or a representative synthetic trace.
- Confirmation of retention requirements and if any requests are considered regulated.
- Point contact for infra + ML (names + calendar availability).

I’ve sketched a migration MAP in the attached spreadsheet (OptiStore-migration-MAP.xlsx) — includes tasks, owners, and an estimated 8–10 week timeline for a conservative cutover. Happy to refine after the deep-dive.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachment: OptiStore-migration-MAP.xlsx (workstreams & timeline)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@optistore.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@optistore.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: OptiStore deployment & migration kickstart

Thanks Dylan + Marissa — this is helpful. Quick answers so you can tune recommendations: 

- Peak traffic: currently ~120 rps, with short bursts up to 160.
- Tokens/day: approximately 2.5M (mixed short/long queries).
- Latency needs: p95 under 300ms for search-oriented queries; longer generative flows can tolerate 1.5s.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII present in a hashed form for analytics flows; payment flows are PCI-scoped but handled by a separate service. SOC2 compliance is required for vendor selection.
- Current infra: we use OpenAI API for most calls, and a legacy on-prem GPU box cluster for heavy tests (slower, inconsistent performance).
- Procurement timeline: target signed PO by 2026-07-30.

Ask: can you provide a ballpark monthly price range for an 8-GPU Dedicated pool vs hosted with a 30% committed discount? Also please add a brief note about how rollback would work if we see quality regressions after model switch.

We can do the technical deep-dive next Tue 23 Jun at 11:00 AM PT — I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

—Olivia
Olivia Chen | Head of ML Platforms | OptiStore

Action items (OptiStore):

- Confirm PoC evaluation criteria (latency, cost/unit, quality thresholds) — Procurement / ML.

I’ve attached the Hosted vs Dedicated comparison and the Redwood security summary for your review (Redwood-Hosted-Dedicated-Comparison.pdf, Redwood-security-summary.pdf). I’ll also include a short rollback pattern: deploy new variant to 10% of traffic, run regression evals against the prompt set, and auto-failover to the prior provider if quality drops exceed your tolerance.

Confirming the deep-dive: Tue 23 Jun 2026, 11:00 AM PT — please accept the calendar invite when you get it. Looking forward to the session.

Thanks,
— Dylan
